policies.policy_name: Mandatory fields validation for incident update
policies.description: Any incident update must include all fields that are mandatory for the operation before calling update_incident.
references: Mandatory Fields: Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields.

policies.policy_name: Role‑based access control for incident updates
policies.description: Only users with the appropriate role may update an incident: Administrators, Managers and Agents have full CRUD on incidents; Reporters may update only incidents they originally submitted.
references: | Administrator (admin) | System Configuration & Integrity | Full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) access across all tables. |

| Manager (manager) | Supervision, Escalation, Approvals | Full CRUD on operational tables (incident, problem, change, knowledge); READ access to all the tables. Can reassign incidents/requests. Can approve/reject Change Requests. Monitors SLAs and escalations. |

| Agent (agent) | Frontline Incident/Request fulfillment | Full CRUD on Incidents, Service Requests, Tasks, Work Notes, CMDB, Change, Problem, and Knowledge. READ access to all the tables. Can update assignment, state, and resolution. | Cannot bypass approvals, or change system administration settings. |

| Reporter (reporter) | IT Service Consumption | Can view and update their own submitted Incidents/Requests. Can search Public Knowledge articles. | Cannot view or modify records opened by other users, CMDB, or internal work notes. |

policies.policy_name: Assignment user must be active Agent or Manager and member of assignment group
policies.description: When the assigned_to field (or assignment_group) is updated, the target user must be active, hold the Agent or Manager role, and belong to the specified assignment group.
references: Constraints: assigned_to must be an active user with the Agent or Manager role and must be a member of the specified assignment_group.

policies.description: The new incident status must follow the allowed state transition matrix before invoking update_incident.
references: new → in_progress / on_hold / resolved
in_progress → on_hold / resolved
on_hold → in_progress (Must log on_hold_reason before transition)
resolved → closed / 'in_progress'

policies.policy_name: Resolution fields required for resolved state
policies.description: If the incident status is being set to resolved, both resolution_code and resolution_notes must be supplied.
references: Resolution Requirement: An Incident cannot transition to resolved without mandatory fields: resolution_code, and resolution_notes (free-form text, max 2000 chars).

policies.policy_name: SLA pause requirement when incident is on hold
policies.description: When status is changed to on_hold, the on_hold_reason must be one of the allowed enumerations and the SLA timer must be set to paused.
references: SLA Pause: The SLA timer must be paused (stage = paused) when the Incident is in stage = on_hold and the on_hold_reason is one of the following enumerations: Awaiting Change, Awaiting Caller, or Awaiting Problem.

policies.description: Any user referenced in the assigned_to field must have users.active = true.
references: User Status: Ensure any user being assigned to (assigned_to) or updated is users.active = true.

policies.policy_name: Referential integrity before closing an incident
policies.description: Before changing an incident’s status to closed, verify that all mandatory dependent records (e.g., resolution notes, linked problem/change) are satisfied.
references: Referential Integrity: Before closing any record, verify that all mandatory dependencies are satisfied.

policies.description: When updating an incident's configuration_item field, only CIs whose status is **in_use** or **maintenance** may be linked. CIs with status **retired** or **disposed** must not be linked to active incidents.
references: CI Status: Only CIs with status = in_use or status = maintenance can be linked to active Incidents. Do not link CIs in status = retired or status = disposed.

policies.description: If the API rate limit is exceeded while invoking **update_incident**, the operation must pause and be retried using exponential back‑off rather than failing immediately.
references: Rate Limiting: If exceeded, pause and retry using Exponential Backoff.

policies.policy_name: Error handling – forbidden and conflict responses
policies.description: When **update_incident** returns a **403 Forbidden** or **409 Conflict**, the assistant must halt the operation and surface the specific error reason to the user.
references: 403 Forbidden: Permission denied (user role lacks authority for the operation).
409 Conflict: Record locking or state conflict.

policies.description: Each call to **update_incident** must be a single, validated operation. The assistant must not combine multiple state changes in one request unless using an approved batch endpoint.
references: Atomic Operations: Perform one validated operation at a time, except when using approved batch endpoints.

policies.policy_name: No assumption or fabrication of identifiers
policies.description: When updating an incident, the assistant must never assume or fabricate IDs, field values, or outcomes; it must rely solely on verified results from the API.
references: Never assume or fabricate IDs, responses, or outcomes — rely solely on verified API results.

policies.policy_name: User clarification for ambiguous or incomplete requests
policies.description: If a request to update an incident is ambiguous or missing mandatory fields, the assistant must not ask for additional information; instead, it must return the list of required fields and indicate which field is missing.
references: User Clarification: Do not ask for further information. If the request is ambiguous, return the list and state the ambiguity. If a mandatory field is missing, state which field is required.

policies.description: If any policy governing incident updates is violated, the assistant must halt the operation immediately and provide the specific policy reason before pausing.
references: Policy Violation: If a user request violates any rule herein, you must halt the operation and provide the specific policy reason before pausing.

policies.description: When creating or updating an incident, the priority field must be derived automatically from the Impact × Urgency matrix; the assistant must not accept a manually supplied priority that conflicts with the system‑calculated value.
references: Priority (critical, high, moderate, low, planning) is determined automatically by the system based on a below pre-defined matrix of Impact x Urgency.
Priority (critical, high, moderate, low, planning) is determined automatically by the system based on a below pre-defined matrix of Impact x Urgency.

policies.description: If the incident is being updated with a resolution_code, the value must be one of the allowed enumerations defined for incidents.
references: incident.resolution_code | fixed, workaround, not_reproducible, closed_by_caller

policies.description: When setting an incident’s status to on_hold (or transitioning from on_hold), the on_hold_reason must be one of the permitted values.
references: incident.on_hold_reason | Awaiting Change, Awaiting Caller, Awaiting Problem

SLA Pause: The SLA timer must be paused (stage = paused) when the Incident is in stage = on_hold and the on_hold_reason is one of the following enumerations: Awaiting Change, Awaiting Caller, or Awaiting Problem.

policies.policy_name: No confirmation required before performing actions
policies.description: The assistant may execute the update_incident operation without asking the user for additional confirmation or permission.
references: You do not need to ask for confirmation or permission before taking action.

policies.description: If any required identifier (e.g., user ID, CI ID) is not supplied, the assistant must first perform a lookup to obtain the correct value before proceeding with the update.
references: When identifiers such as names or IDs are missing, perform lookups, verify that you are reusing correct values from previous responses, and proceed using the retrieved data.

policies.description: The assistant must never expose or return data that lies outside the authenticated user’s access scope when processing an incident update.
references: Knowledge Scope: Do not disclose information that is outside the authenticated user's access scope.

policies.description: If an incident’s SLA timer enters the breached stage, the assistant must set the incident’s escalation flag to true and trigger an automatic notification to the Manager.
references: Breach: If the SLA exceeds its duration (stage = breached), the escalation flag on the Incident must be set to true, and an automatic notification sent to the Manager.

policies.policy_name: Verified user role and record relationship enforcement
policies.description: Before invoking **update_incident**, the assistant must confirm the requesting user's role and ensure the user‑record relationship is verified according to the ITIL/database integrity rules.
references: First you must check the user information and operate exclusively based on confirmed user roles, verified record relationships, and ITIL/database integrity rules.

policies.description: When updating an incident, the assistant must never bypass any required approvals (e.g., change or problem approvals) that are mandated by the ITSM process.
references: You are strictly prohibited from assuming data, executing ambiguous commands, bypassing mandatory approvals, or violating audit and compliance requirements.

policies.policy_name: Audit logging of user actions (time tracking) for incident updates
policies.description: All updates to an incident must be recorded as a work log that includes the timestamp (**created_on**) and the **user_id** of the person performing the update.
references: Time Tracking: All work logs must include the timestamp (created_on) and the user_id performing the action.
